implemented_requirements.requirement: Tetrominoes fall from the top of the board
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update() advances a gravity timer and calls try_move(0,1) which moves the current Tetromino down; initial y is 0 in Tetromino.__init__ (tetromino.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can move left/right, soft drop, hard drop, and rotate pieces before they land
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.handle_keydown() maps LEFT/RIGHT to try_move(-1,0)/try_move(1,0), DOWN to soft drop (try_move + score), SPACE to hard_drop(), and UP to try_rotate() (game.py).
Board.clear_lines() removes full rows and returns the count; called in Game.lock_current_piece() after locking a piece.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring increases for line clears, soft drops, and hard drops
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.lock_current_piece() adds LINE_SCORES based on cleared lines; Game.handle_keydown() adds SOFT_DROP_SCORE for each soft drop; Game.hard_drop() adds HARD_DROP_SCORE per row dropped.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when no more pieces can be placed
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.lock_current_piece() sets self.game_over = True if board.lock_piece reports overflow or board.is_valid_position(self.next_piece) is False.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board updates after each move or drop
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.grid is modified in Board.lock_piece(); Game.update() calls draw() each frame which renders the current board state via ui.draw_board().

implemented_requirements.requirement: All seven standard Tetromino shapes are included
implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.SHAPES defines I, O, T, S, Z, J, L; PieceBag shuffles SHAPES.keys() ensuring each appears.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop speed increases as the game progresses
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._drop_interval(level) computes interval using BASE_DROP_INTERVAL and DROP_SPEEDUP_FACTOR; level is increased in lock_current_piece() based on lines cleared.

critical_issues: The initial spawn of the first piece is not validated; if the board is already filled at reset, game_over may not be set until the next lock.
The code assumes pygame is installed; missing dependency would prevent execution.
judge.summary: The provided source files implement a functional Tetris game meeting the core benchmark requirements: falling tetrominoes, player controls, line clearing, scoring, game‑over detection, all seven shapes, and progressive speed increase. The implementation is largely complete and appears runnable with pygame, though initial spawn validation and external dependency handling are minor gaps.
